SSW-OHS-007-PRC REV2 Corrective Maintenance 1. PURPOSE Corrective Maintenance includes any corrective actions needed to fix or repair any issues found during the normal operation of the sites working. This may vary for a number of different reasons and instances. The CM Field Engineer/Team should carry enough spares in their vehicle to effect local repairs whenever possible. Where major components or follow up work is required on a site, a CM Trouble Ticket should be opened along with a SIT ticket. In order to ensure equipment and facilities optimum performance one should consider the best equipment and facilitate periodic inspections to be carried out in addition to regular preventive maintenance. In order to meet the minimum downtime requirements for the equipment and in order to achieve optimal operating performance a swiftly deployed highly skilled and equipped emergency repair team is required. 2. SCOPE All equipment and facilities must be inspected and tested to ensure operating conditions are sustained. This will include verification of equipment performance, identification of any fault and miss matching operational behavior of the equipment. Replacement of worn parts as prescribed from the original equipment manufacturer to meet the recommended global standard. In order to ensure equipment can provide the optimal performance efficiency it will require that equipment to operate at the lowest downtime possible. To achieve the optimal performance the equipment failure must be attended immediately and restored to its normal operating condition. Through the process one will require a detailed analysis to identify the root cause of the component failure, replacing faulty components and inspecting and testing the equipment for the normal operating condition. These checks should be carried out in accordance with the Sincro Sitewatch Quality Operating Systems Manual. 3. REFERENCES Sincro will ensure all corrective maintenance at site is carried out with respect to the client specifications. Sincro will ensure an equipment reference manual is provided to all CM teams as reference and guideline for CM activities compliance check. Also, the CM compliance must include:  Minimum List of spare parts per CM Vehicle, the extent and content of this list may change from time to time as new equipment is added  Minimum list of tools in tool boxes and supplementary items e.g. compressed air blowing machines, electric drills, software interface tools, the list of tools required may change from time to time as new equipment is added. SSW-OHS-007-PRC REV2 Corrective Maintenance 4. DEFINITIONS CM: Corrective Maintenance PM: Preventive Maintenance NOC: Network Operation Centre SINCRO: Sincro Sitewatch Limited HSE: Health, Safety and Environment FT: Field Technician (CM Team) OP : Operation Manager. FS: Field Supervisor ZOH Zone Operation Head IR: Inspection and Test Request 5. RESPONSIBILITIES  Sincro determines that CM compliance is the responsibility of all individuals within the company including members of the senior management team as well as the field supervisory and operational teams.  Sincro management will insure the teams involved in CM activities will be equipped with all necessary tools and materials to ensure the minimum KPI target is exceeded  Sincro will insure all CM execution activities are carried out in accordance with client and our EHS prescribed procedures this includes the use of proper working tools, qualified personnel, risk assessment, PPE etc.  Sincro will ensure the CM team will attend all CM activities within the specified schedule time and exceed the KPI target.  Sincro will insure that the most common required spare parts and materials for CM activities are available either in the vehicle in the case of fast moving spares or at local stores in the region in the case of non-predictable items  Sincro will ensure all spares and materials used in performing CM activities are all genuine spares parts and meet the OEM recommendation.  Sincro will ensure each CM team undergoes capacity training to match technological change and gain the best practice in all services the company offers.  While onsite to carry out CM activities, the technicians responsible should observe the general site condition, and raise a TT ticket with the NOC for any follow up actions accordingly, unless they themselves can resolve the issues immediately.  Sincro will ensure their teams take all necessary data and records whilst attending site such as Fuel and Luku levels as are required by existing protocols, such protocols may update from to time. 6.0 EQUIPMENT Sincro CM teams will be equipped with appropriate standard tools and equipment to carry out all works to meet and exceed the required KPI target. The CM team will be provided with tools and equipment as required to ensure the technical competence which includes but is not limited to:  Complete electrical and mechanical toolbox including AC/DC multimeter with Page 4 of 6

SSW-OHS-007-PRC REV2 Corrective Maintenance temperature probe  Suitable vehicle typically 4x4 1 tonne field pick up of a make and type that is suitable to the road infrastructure in the locality served  Laptop computer  Smart phone.  Spare parts and replacement service parts as per scheduled lists  Software interface tools  PPE and additional safety equipment as may be required 7. PROCEDURE  CM team to be ready in responding to all alarms as escalated from the NOC team.  CM team must report the estimated time of arrival site immediate after alarm notification at all times and provide the CM plan to the customer as required.  CM team to request site access permit in accordance with required procedures.  CM team to attend all fault incidents as escalated from NOC and close them immediately as required in the SLA MTTR.  CM team to carry out all CM to a technical standard as required by original equipment manufacturers.  CM team will carry out all corrective measures on site and ensure no fault will result from their failure to perform best procedure in repairing any fault on site.  CM team to record all materials and spares used during CM activities and report to the specific departments as required in escalation procedure.  CM team to remove all waste from the CM activities as required by HSE procedure  CM team to report all additional works as may be required for restoring the site to optimum condition as required by CM and escalation procedure.  CM team to report all current site information as required in PM and CM protocols and escalation procedures.  CM team to check for and report any issues where HSE and Security is compromised on the site.
